title: Atmospheric Layers Explorer
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: See the atmosphere drawn to honest scale, discover how thin the weather-producing layer really is, then stretch the troposphere to read the detail inside it.

learningObjectives: Interpret a scale drawing of the atmosphere to explain where weather occurs.
Recognise how thin the weather-producing layer is compared to the whole atmosphere.
prerequisites: Knowing that air gets thinner with altitude
Reading a value off a vertical scale

keyQuestions: If the troposphere is only 12 km deep, why does the sky look infinite?
Why can a thunderstorm not punch into the stratosphere?
Is the International Space Station in the atmosphere or above it?
commonMisconceptions: Believing the atmosphere ends at a sharp boundary.
Assuming temperature falls continuously all the way up.
Thinking space begins immediately above the clouds.
assessmentOpportunities: States that essentially all weather occurs in the bottom 12 km.
Explains why storms flatten out at the tropopause instead of continuing upward.
Reads pressure and temperature off the slider and relates them to a familiar altitude.
